findings.reason: sealing one exposed root while the identical grant exposes its sibling leaves a worker able to destroy the plan's own review evidence, so the fix must seal both roots, not the reports root alone.
findings.text: §10 seals only the reports root, but `_fence_write_roots` in reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py passes `review_store_directory=review_store_root()` into the same `delivery_write_roots` call, so every fenced launch also gets the whole of `~/.config/reckon/crew/reviews` writable; the deleting run's own worker.json argv binds `/home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/reviews` writable beside `.../crew/reports`, so any worker can still `rm -rf` the store of every project's review records

findings.reason: a done-when clause that cannot fail gives a node dispatched at §10 no falsifier that review records survive the change, and hides the omitted root behind a check that always passes.
findings.text: §10's done-when asserts that "a run review whose delivery path lies under the review store ... still write their records", but the section seals only the reports root, which never touches `crew/reviews`, so that clause holds however the code behaves and is no control for the seal
